Name: Pick Your Enchantment Restored
Author: focustense
Description:
[color=#ffdd96][size=6]Pick Your Enchantment[/size][/color]

[i]"1000g, a stack of healing/buff items and an hour of grinding for a single RNG chance? No thanks."[/i]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Introduction[/size][/color]

Tool/weapon enchantments in Stardew Valley are randomized, but can be manipulated with some cheap tricks, such as careful tool/enchantment ordering and throwaway enchants. Even if you don't use a predictor and don't know what you're doing, it's still possible to get the result you want through trial-and-error and save scumming. Since it's already possible, but merely tedious and irritating, this mod removes the tedious and irritating part and simply lets you pick the enchantment you want.

Place your tool or weapon in the forge's left slot, and a prismatic shard in the right slot, and use the arrows to select your new enchantment!

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]History[/size][/color]

This mod is a continuation of the original [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/11376]Pick Your Enchantment[/url] mod, posted with permission* from Atravita. It adds support for Stardew Valley 1.6 and removes the dependency on AtraCore. Aside from that, it is simply a maintenance update; I do not have a list of new features planned.

[size=1]* To slightly paraphrase his exact words: [i]"Please, take it off my hands. If even one more person asks me when I'm releasing a 1.6 update then there is going to be a face-shaped hole in my desk."[/i] Seriously, don't bug him if you find issues with this mod.[/size]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Installation[/size][/color]

Pick Your Enchantment follows the standard installation procedure for most mods:

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI and set up your game for mods, per the [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Player_Guide/Getting_Started]Modding: Player's Guide[/url] instructions.
[*]Download the main file from the Files tab.
[*]Open the .zip file and extract the [font=Courier New]ForgeMenuChoice[/font] folder into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley\Mods[/font] folder.
[*]Launch the game!
[/list]
[color=#ffe599][size=5]Configuration[/size][/color]

All of this mod's options are configurable through GMCM. If you prefer to edit the [font=Courier New]config.json[/font] or are having any trouble with the in-game settings, read on for a detailed explanation of what the settings do.

[b]Example Configuration[/b]

[font=Courier New]{
"TooltipBehavior": "Immersive",
"EnableTooltipAutogeneration": true,
"LeftArrow": "LeftShoulder, Left",
"RightArrow": "RightShoulder, Right",
"OverrideInnateEnchantments": false
}[/font]

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Settings[/size][/color]

[list]
[*][font=Courier New][b]TooltipBehavior[/b][/font]: Controls whether tooltips are displayed on mouse hover. Options are: [font=Courier New]On[/font], [font=Courier New]Off[/font], or [font=Courier New]Immersive[/font], where [font=Courier New]Immersive [/font](default) only makes the tooltips appear if any farmer has seen Journal Scrap 8.
[*][font=Courier New][b]EnableTooltipAutogeneration[/b][/font]: the data for the tooltips is parsed from Journal Scrap 8; if you have a mod that edits that, you may want to disable tooltips or remove automatic tooltip generation.
[*][font=Courier New][b]OverrideInnateEnchantments[/b][/font]: Toggles whether or not [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Forge#Innate_enchantments]Innate Enchantments[/url]﻿ can also be selected. Only one innate can be selected at a time, and it will replace [i]all[/i] previous innates; this means you can consistently put "good" innates on a weapon, but if you want the very [i]best[/i] combinations of innates (e.g. min-maxing) then you'll have to disable this and submit to the RNG.
[*][b][font=Courier New]LeftArrow[/font] [/b]and [b][font=Courier New]RightArrow[/font] [/b]change the key bindings to select the previous/next available enchantment. By default they include [font=Courier New]LeftShoulder[/font] and [font=Courier New]RightShoulder[/font] to support gamepads.
[/list]
[color=#ffe599][size=5]Patching (for mod authors)[/size][/color]

Pick Your Enchantment provides a few options for authors of forge/enchantment mods to add their own compatibility, using either SMAPI or Content Patcher:

[list]
[*]Re-skins can replace the menu textures by patching [font=Courier New]Mods/atravita_ForgeMenuChoice_Forge_Buttons[/font].
[*]Tooltips for vanilla enchantments are automatically generated by inspecting Journal Scrap 9. Mods that change vanilla descriptions or add new enchantment types can patch [font=Courier New]Mods/atravita_ForgeMenuChoice_Tooltip_Data[/font].
[/list]
[i][b]Note:[/b] The asset paths are intentionally unchanged from the original (Atravita) mod in order to maintain backward compatibility with mods that already patch these assets.[/i]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Uninstall[/size][/color]

Why would you want to do that?

But if you must, simply delete the mod from your Mods directory.

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Compatibility[/size][/color]

[i][size=1]Note: Atravita was extremely conscientious about mod compatibility. I am not. SMAPI and Harmony allow mod authors make any arbitrary changes they want to the game's code, which means every compatibility patch is potentially a bespoke implementation for every combination of versions. I will therefore make every effort to support compatibility with "typical" mod lists that don't radically alter gameplay, but don't plan to add compatibility features for every other mod out there and maintain them in perpetuity. You're welcome to ask, of course; just don't expect an immediate or entirely satisfying answer.[/size][/i]

Current compatibility:

[list]
[*]Works with Stardew Valley 1.6 on Linux/macOS/Windows.
[*]Works in single player, multiplayer, and split-screen mode. Should be fine if installed for one player only.
[*]Majority of popular mods (e.g. SpaceCore, and mods using it to add forge recipes) will be compatible.
[*]This version is [b]not[/b] compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10668]Enchantable Scythes[/url]﻿. Compatibility [b]may[/b] be restored in the future.
[*]Other mods that do any of the following may have various degrees of incompatibility:
[list]
[*]Changing the Forge menu's layout or overall appearance
[*]Modifying vanilla enchantments or recipes
[*]Changing the behavior of melee weapons or adding new weapons with novel behavior.
[/list][/list]
[color=#ffe599][size=5]Questions/Bugs?[/size][/color]

Feel free to either:

[list][*]Create a [url=https://github.com/focustense/StardewForgeMenuChoice/issues]GitHub issue[/url]; when doing so, please follow bug-reporting etiquette. Check first for similar reports, and make sure to include all relevant details about your issue, especially including clear repro steps and/or [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log[/url].
[*]Or, ping me on the [url=https://discord.com/invite/stardewvalley]SV Discord[/url] if I happen to be around. Discord is best if you have a quick question, but I make no promises re: availability for in-depth troubleshooting. [i](DMs will be ignored.)[/i]
[/list]
As is my policy, comments/posts on Nexus will always be open so that community members can support each other when I’m on modding hiatus, but I will probably not see them nor respond. GitHub and Discord are my only two communication channels.
